assertions.assert: It is ready once both its children, the conversation and speaking, are ready (their first `bot.ability.offers`): on every entry into active it sends `bot.ability.offers` `{ability: "communication", choices}`, choices the one model-callable `bot.ability.communication.respond` with its schema compacted (no `$schema`, title or examples), no target.

`bot.ability.communication.input` in active goes to the conversation; a text product comes back to the body as `bot.ability.cognition.input` `{stimulus}` unchanged, its stimulus carrying the conversation's history with the input as its latest, inbound, message.
A product that is not text reaches the body as the conversation's `bot.ability.conversation.output` itself (its latest message inbound); history whose latest message is outbound is not forwarded.
A conversation that cannot take an input fails it: its `bot.ability.conversation.failed` `{stage, message}` goes on to the body unchanged.

`bot.ability.communication.respond` `{text}` (non-blank) in active is said through speaking: the body gets speaking's playout in order, `bot.ability.speaking.efference` `{mouth: "speaking", duration, media_type, sample_rate_hz, channels}` then `environment.sound` `{audio, media_type, sample_rate_hz, channels, source: "speaking"}`, then `bot.ability.speaking.output` `{text, media_type, sample_rate_hz, channels}`; the communication is active again and offers again, and the outbound record goes to the conversation as history only.
A blank response answers `bot.ability.communication.failed` `{message: "Communication response text must be non-blank."}` without speaking; the communication stays active and says the next response.
A speaking failure answers `bot.ability.communication.failed` `{message}` (speaking's failure message) and the communication is active again.

A response is bounded by `response_timeout_ms` (36000 by default, a `<param>`: speaking's 30 s encoding bound plus the original's 6 s): when it passes before speaking answers, the body gets `bot.ability.communication.failed` `{message: "Speaking response timed out."}` and the communication is active again; speaking's late answer is not forwarded. `encoding_timeout_ms` (30000 by default, a `<param>`; decision D98) is passed to speaking as its encoding bound.
Responses and input that arrive while a response is in hand, and input that arrives before it is active, are deferred and taken, in order, once it is active.
`bot.ability.communication.activate` `{}` is taken only in inactive: in active it does nothing.
